didYouKnow: 1 in 2 adults with diabetes remain undiagnosed — over 263 million people worldwide.
95% of diabetes growth through 2050 is projected in low- and middle-income countries.

Type 1 diabetes affects 1.9 million children and adolescents under age 20 globally.

faq.q: How many people have diabetes worldwide in 2026?
faq.a: Based on the IDF Diabetes Atlas 11th Edition, an estimated 589 million adults aged 20-79 were living with diabetes in 2024, representing 11.1% of the global adult population. This figure is projected to reach 853 million by 2050.

faq.q: What percentage of diabetes cases are undiagnosed?
faq.a: Approximately 44.7% of all diabetes cases globally are undiagnosed, meaning over 263 million adults are living with diabetes without knowing it.

faq.q: Which country has the highest diabetes prevalence?
faq.a: Pakistan currently has the highest age-standardized diabetes prevalence at approximately 30.8%, followed by French Polynesia and Kuwait.

faq.q: What is the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes?
faq.a: Type 1 is an autoimmune condition (~10% of cases) requiring insulin. Type 2 (~90%) involves insulin resistance and is largely preventable through lifestyle changes.

faq.q: How many people die from diabetes each year?
faq.a: Diabetes was responsible for approximately 3.4 million deaths in 2024 — equivalent to one death every 9 seconds.
